items.item: the pod index is published via the downward API into the JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX environment variable
both per-index backoff limits and Job success policy are announced as GA in the 1.33 release

backoffLimitPerIndex and maxFailedIndexes answer two different questions — one caps retries within an index, the other caps how many indexes may fail before the whole Job is cut short early — and conflating them is the single easiest mistake to make reading this feature for the first time

at.deep: Two different caps, one easy mix-up

items.item: when backoffLimitPerIndex is set, spec.backoffLimit itself silently defaults to MaxInt32 instead of 6, which is what lets per-index retries actually run their own course instead of being cut off by the old shared counter

a podFailurePolicy field requires the pod template to set restartPolicy: Never, or the API rejects the Job outright — a validation requirement easy to trip over when adding a failure policy to an existing Job

at.out: a specific API validation detail, named in post-notes's code-review section rather than dramatized in the reel

items.item: FailIndex, the fourth pod-failure-policy action, exists specifically to pair with per-index backoff — it fails one index outright on a matched condition, skipping that index's remaining retries, without touching the others

at.step: Classify the failure, not just count it

items.item: unmanaged Jobs (created directly, not through a CronJob) default to an orphanDependents deletion policy, which is exactly why the docs themselves recommend always setting ttlSecondsAfterFinished rather than relying on manual cleanup
concurrencyPolicy only ever compares a CronJob's own runs against each other — multiple different CronJobs are always allowed to run concurrently regardless of any one's policy

a suspended CronJob (spec.suspend: true) still counts its skipped executions as missed jobs, and turning suspension back off without a starting deadline schedules all of them immediately — a surprising interaction with the missed-schedule rule

at.out: a documented interaction narrower than this topic's concurrency/missed-schedule running example; named here for a future seam, not taught in the reel

items.item: the CronJob controller checks for missed schedules on a fixed internal interval, which is why a startingDeadlineSeconds set below that interval can cause the CronJob not to be scheduled at all

at.out: an operational caveat below this topic's scope

items.item: the batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp annotation (added in v1.32) records a Job's originally scheduled time, separate from its actual creation time, which is what makes auditing a Replace-policy CronJob's history possible after the fact

at.out: a recent annotation below this topic's scope, named for a future seam

items.item: the Job doc's own note that terminating pods are not counted as failures until they reach a terminal phase (when a podFailurePolicy is set) is the same mechanism that makes the brief two-pods-one-index overlap possible — the replacement starts before the terminal phase is confirmed
